cases.scenario: Two selections may overlap. Selection A starts first, selection B becomes current, B completes, then A completes. Determine whether older work can still overwrite state owned by B.
Operations execute through one serialized queue. Operation B cannot start until operation A has completed or failed, and only the queue owner mutates the projection.

View A schedules requestAnimationFrame work. Navigation replaces A with view B before the callback runs. The callback still dereferences a shared current DOM ref and mutates it without checking view identity.
A view schedules delayed measurement work. Cleanup cancels the handle, and the callback also checks the exact render generation before touching the DOM.
One publish operation first commits metadata in the database and then writes the content file. If the file write fails, the committed metadata remains visible as published although no content exists.

A multi-step import uses explicit durable states PREPARING, READY, and FAILED. Readers only consume READY, restart resumes or cleans PREPARING deterministically, and every intermediate state is part of the documented workflow.

A queue may redeliver the same message after acknowledgement timeout. Each delivery sends the notification and inserts a history row using the same operation id, but neither effect has a duplicate guard.

Redelivery is expected. The effect owner performs a create-only write keyed by the logical operation id, returns the existing terminal result on duplicate delivery, and does not repeat external effects.

A request acquires a temporary directory and starts a child process that still reads from it after the request handler returns. The handler's finally block deletes the directory before the child signals completion.
A process-wide immutable schema registry is created once at startup, owned by the process lifetime, never closed by request code, and released only during process shutdown.
A storage timeout is thrown by the repository, converted to None by one service, interpreted as not-found by the API, but treated as retryable by a worker that calls the repository directly.

The domain returns one explicit NotFound result. The HTTP boundary maps it once to 404, the worker maps the same stable result to a terminal receipt, and neither boundary changes its semantic meaning.
The API layer and worker layer both decide the same can-run policy from the same raw configuration. There is no documented distinction between the two decisions.
Admission decides eligibility once. Persistence later verifies that the admitted identity still matches the stored record but does not reinterpret eligibility.
An API cancellation handler writes terminal status directly. Worker cleanup contains a separate direct write that can mark the same operation cancelled using its own conditions.
Inspect whether this example has multiple independent durable transition authorities. Ignore unrelated asynchronous ordering defects.
Admission resolves and returns a canonical repository identity. Execution receives both that identity and the raw path, ignores the identity, and resolves ownership again from the path.
Inspect whether a previously resolved fact is discarded and reconstructed from raw inputs. Do not report simple duplicate policy logic unless a resolved-result boundary was actually crossed backward.
A database row and a writable process cache can both update lifecycle status. Reads sometimes prefer the cache and sometimes the database, with no declared canonical owner or freshness rule.
The database is explicitly canonical. An immutable receipt records the historical terminal outcome and is never read as current mutable state.

A model independently stores status, cancelled, completed_at, and result. It can represent status=running, cancelled=true, completed_at set, and a success result at the same time although the domain forbids that combination.
Several optional metadata fields are independent observations. Every combination is valid in the domain and no downstream branch must repair contradictory lifecycle meaning.
One command walks an include graph and reads every module to validate it. Planning later receives the source root rather than the graph, walks the includes again, and rereads the same modules.
Two separate user commands run minutes apart. Each command independently scans the repository because each is a distinct logical operation with its own observation boundary.

A route calls a helper, which calls a service, which calls a facade. Each layer forwards the same values and errors unchanged to the existing domain owner and adds no invariant, protocol conversion, transaction, or trust boundary.
A thin adapter converts a public HTTP payload into a validated domain command and prevents untrusted fields from crossing the boundary.
All current execution uses admittedRun.execute(), except one remaining caller that still invokes legacyDirectExecute() with equivalent supported semantics and bypasses the canonical owner.
Two entry paths remain because one performs an interactive dry run and the other performs a durable production execution. Their contracts and effects are intentionally different.
A function named getCurrentProfile() reads the profile and, as an undocumented part of the getter, persists a last_seen timestamp and emits an event.
A command named recordProfileAccess() explicitly documents and performs the durable write and event emission at the application boundary.
A validator receives a 30-field application context, reads two fields, and forwards most of the remainder through three layers solely because the context type is used everywhere.
A cohesive Order aggregate has many fields, but its validation invariant genuinely depends on most of them and callers treat the aggregate as one domain concept.
A test asserting one local normalization rule enters the public production API, which always performs a full repository scan and starts a subprocess before reaching the normalization.
Inspect whether this test is slow because it performs disproportionate production work. Ignore nondeterministic waiting if that is the actual issue.
Forty small logic tests each construct the same expensive application graph, rebuild repository indexes, and initialize unrelated services because the production object cannot be cheaply constructed.
Each persistence integration test creates a clean database because isolation of transaction and constraint semantics is exactly what the suite is proving.
A deterministic tax calculation cannot be invoked without starting a database and HTTP server because the only production API bundles loading, networking, persistence, and calculation together.
The test explicitly verifies transaction isolation and the HTTP serialization contract, so the database and server are part of the behavior under test.

To prove one narrow cancellation rule, a test constructs five subsystems, patches internal callbacks, drives four lifecycle states, coordinates cleanup, and asserts private intermediate state from each subsystem.
A single end-to-end test intentionally verifies a workflow whose public contract spans those same five subsystems; lower-level tests already cover their individual rules.
Inspect how the test knows background work is complete before it asserts.
The test holds a barrier, starts the worker, releases the barrier at a deterministic point, waits on the worker's explicit completion promise, and then asserts.
A mutable module-global cache survives between tests. Running test B alone passes, but running test A before B changes B's result unless a broad reset fixture clears the cache.
Tests share an immutable parsed schema object. No test can mutate it and execution order does not change any result.
A behavior-preserving refactor breaks tests because they assert the exact order of three private helper calls and patch internal module functions rather than observing the public result.
A structural test fails when UI modules import the persistence client directly because that import boundary is an explicit architecture invariant.

A repository hotspot contains repeated include-graph reads and the same eligibility rule independently implemented in two production layers. Identify which narrow specialist reviews should inspect the evidence next.
The request already names stale-work-race-review and provides the exact asynchronous path and ownership evidence to inspect. No discovery or routing decision is needed.

There is a real stale asynchronous overwrite in this fixture. Determine whether that also means the durable transition has multiple independent commit authorities. Report only this skill's failure class.

There is duplicate policy interpretation in this fixture. Determine whether any already-resolved semantic result is discarded so downstream code moves backward to raw inputs. Report only this skill's failure class.

The fixture contains a weak timing synchronization technique. Determine whether the test also performs disproportionate production work relative to the behavior it proves. Report only this skill's failure class.

The same queue message with the same logical operation id is delivered twice because acknowledgement timed out. No newer owner or superseding operation exists; the concern is duplicate execution of the same operation.
One canonical publish owner performs two required writes. A crash between them leaves partial state. There is only one semantic transition authority and one commit path.

A React view schedules RAF work that runs after navigation replaces the view. The defect is specifically old view-generation work acting on the replacement UI; no general resource acquisition/release contract is involved.

A storage timeout is converted to None in one layer and treated as not-found, while another caller treats the same timeout as retryable. The disputed semantic fact is specifically failure meaning and retryability.
A proof identity hashes a list of evidence anchors in caller-provided order. Reversing the same unordered anchors changes the identity even though the semantic evidence set is identical.
A pipeline-stage identity changes when the ordered stage sequence changes because execution order is explicitly part of the semantic contract.

The canonical evidence packet records an explicitly changed CSS file as missing. The compact projection filters missing rows out entirely, and downstream callers cannot distinguish missing evidence from a file that was never reported.
A UI summary intentionally shows only actionable rows, labels itself as a partial view, exposes truncation/exclusion counts, and all authority decisions consume the complete canonical packet instead.

A search layer returns the highest-ranked edit candidate with no ownership proof. A later brief converts any non-null candidate into owner_resolved=true without adding structural, explicit, or scoped proof.
A candidate becomes authoritative only after a separate validator proves an exact owner within a declared complete proof scope and records that proof identity.
A streaming importer reports complete when parser_failures==0. Its last record lacks a trailing newline and is never counted as selected, processed, failed, excluded, or missing.
A bounded scan reports selected=100, processed=96, excluded=2, malformed=1, missing=1 and sets complete only because the terminal categories reconcile exactly to 100.
The same repository/task resolves owner A at limit=10 but owner B at limit=100 solely because more presentation candidates are visible; neither result records new authoritative proof.
Increasing top-k reveals more related candidates but the proven owner and proof identity remain unchanged; only bounded presentation completeness changes.
A task-analysis cache key contains task text and limit but not repository generation. After source changes, the same key returns the previous owner's result.
A derived cache key binds repository generation, task, policy and limits; persisted payloads are content-hash verified and the cache is disposable.
An integer wider than SQLite's signed range is stored through a float-compatible column. Reopening the database silently changes the exact revision number and therefore the reconstructed identity.
Out-of-range metadata uses a canonical checked codec; reopen reproduces the exact integers and malformed/non-canonical persisted bytes fail explicitly.
A PASS receipt identity binds command output but omits repository source identity and execution mode, so a receipt from different bytes and a simulation run can be reused as native proof.
A reusable receipt identity binds repository/source, task, policy, generation, producer schema, execution mode and environment dimensions that affect interpretation.
A missing ranking metric is loaded with value = payload.get('ndcg') or 0.0. Qualification then treats unmeasured ranking as a measured zero instead of unknown evidence.
The model stores metric_value separately from metric_status, preserving unknown, stale, invalid and measured-zero as distinct serialized states.
Qualification averages correctness, speed and cost. One false-authority result scores zero, but excellent speed/cost raise the weighted average above the PASS threshold.
Qualification rejects any false-authority violation first, then evaluates readiness, and only afterward uses soft ranking/economics metrics to compare otherwise valid runs.

A before/after debt report claims -40 findings, but the after run uses different Ruff thresholds and excludes a source directory; the delta code never checks configuration or source-universe identity.
Two runs have matching metric definition, tool/config identity, source universe, execution mode and population; their receipts share the same comparability identity before a delta is computed.
A benchmark with zero active qualification cases reports PASS because it has zero violations. Its only rows are historical shadow cases and required ambiguity/non-edit slices are absent.
Scoring begins only after the corpus proves non-empty active valid qualification membership, adjudicated ground truth and coverage of every required semantic slice.

For the same source generation and task, the Python API reports ownership unresolved while the compact CLI brief marks the same candidate safe to edit. The CLI adapter reinterprets candidate presence locally.
API, CLI and MCP use different field names and formatting, but after removing presentation-only fields they expose the same candidate, ambiguity, authority, freshness and provenance state.
Adding an unrelated documentation file changes the selected owner for an exact-symbol task even though the new file is outside the task proof scope and contributes no owner evidence.
Adding unrelated files and equivalent task wording leaves the conclusion unchanged, while removing the exact owner symbol changes the result to unresolved as expected.

A repository hit is tagged visibility=deny. Retrieval hides it from the raw list, but owner resolution still receives the unfiltered hit collection and uses the denied exact symbol as ownership proof.

Visibility policy filters denied evidence at the canonical evidence boundary before ranking, caches, projections or authority logic; an authorized privileged surface uses a separate explicitly scoped request.

A pull request adds 20 lint violations and raises the checked-in allowed-debt baseline by 20. CI validates live debt only against the modified baseline, so the regression passes without comparing the baseline to previous main.
CI first compares the candidate baseline to previous main and permits only independently allowed downward ratchets, then validates candidate code against that admitted baseline.

The task names package.module.evaluate. The repository contains one exact module-level evaluate symbol, but owner selection ignores the module qualifier and replaces it with a structurally related helper from another module.
A literal path resolves uniquely and remains the edit target; related dependencies stay related evidence, while ownership authority remains unresolved until separate proof is available.

A change to package/runtime/parser.py selects a generic repository-tools test with no reference evidence, while package/runtime/test_parser.py directly imports and exercises the changed function. Generic retrieval rank wins anyway.
The selected integration test is broader than a nearby unit test but has direct reference evidence to the changed public behavior and is therefore the stronger verifier.

A function creates env = os.environ.copy(), reads env, then updates env. A concurrency review requires a global lock solely because the values originated from os.environ, even though the fresh mapping never escapes the function.
Two worker threads mutate the same process-wide cache object through aliases. The cache has one explicit lock owner and every mutation crosses that synchronization boundary.

The core API accepts a 900 KiB evidence packet and documents it as reusable as previous_state, but the transport endpoint caps requests at 512 KiB. A fully valid core result therefore cannot be round-tripped through the supported API.
Core and transport share one 512 KiB semantic payload bound. A documented compact transform exists for larger diagnostic views and explicitly marks itself partial and non-authoritative.

A previous evidence packet carries sha256:abc. A caller mutates nested evidence but leaves the digest field unchanged; delta code trusts the stored digest and compares the tampered packet without recomputing canonical identity.
Every serialized or externally supplied evidence artifact is canonically rehashed at the reuse boundary and rejected before interpretation when content does not match the claimed identity.
Events have serial numbers unique only per producer. Aggregation uses serial alone as a global dictionary key, so producer A serial 42 overwrites producer B serial 42.
Serial numbers are documented as stream-local and only used inside one stream; cross-stream aggregation uses producer_id plus serial as the composite identity and rejects duplicate composite keys.
A bounded dependency scan of the first 100 nodes returns no owner. completeness is caller-claimed complete but truncation is unknown, and downstream code concludes that no owner exists anywhere.
No-owner is admitted only after the declared repository scope is fully enumerated, completeness=complete and truncation=complete; bounded or unknown scans remain unknown.

One status enum uses SAFE_FRESH, SAFE_STALE and UNSAFE to encode both repository freshness and ownership resolution. It cannot represent fresh-but-ambiguous evidence separately from stale-but-resolved ownership.
freshness, ownership_status and completeness are independent fields; a UI may derive a summary badge from them, but authority decisions use the primitive axes.
A cleanup selector sorts last month's checked-in debt baseline and chooses the largest entry as today's hotspot even though the executable current inventory no longer contains that file.
The checked-in baseline is used only as a no-growth ratchet. A fresh executable inventory measured from current source/config selects the cleanup target and is then compared with the baseline.
A complex function is split into three helpers and the PR claims structural-debt reduction. Focused tests pass, but fresh post-edit debt remains exactly unchanged and no locality metric improved.
A refactor claims behavior preservation only until comparable post-edit measurement shows debt 69→31 with no redistribution and the frozen behavior suite still passes.

A decision reads repository candidates at generation 10, a file changes, then verification evidence is read at generation 11. The result is emitted as one decision packet with no generation mismatch marker.
All component reads in the decision bind generation 10; if any stable read detects a revision change, the decision is retried or fails without emitting a mixed-generation packet.
A static call analyzer sees obj.save() where obj is dynamically supplied and marks it as an exact call to repository class Store.save, despite having no type or alias proof for the receiver.
Exact calls are emitted only for lexically or index-proven targets; dynamic receivers and imported external methods remain dynamic/external or ambiguous rather than exact repository facts.

A runtime error anchor and a dependency-upgrade observation both correlate to the same repository module. The system automatically labels the upgrade as the cause and selects that dependency for remediation.
The system reports same-repository-target correspondence and preserves dependency/runtime provenance, while causation and remediation remain not-inferred for a separate consumer to adjudicate.

An external /app/src prefix maps to the repository root. The mapper accepts /app/src/../secrets.txt, normalizes after joining, and produces a path outside the repository while still labeling it repository evidence.

Path mapping chooses the deterministic longest matching prefix, rejects .. traversal, resolves symlinks/realpath, then re-checks that the final canonical path remains beneath the declared repository root.

A branch repairs three evidence-backed in-scope defects and all known regressions pass. It immediately runs final CI and opens a PR. No fresh adversarial dogfood pass challenges the patched behavior after the latest repair.

After repairing a boundary bug, the campaign declares six required probes. Two difficult probes time out, so after seeing the results it removes those two from the required set, records NO_QUALIFYING_DEFECT, and claims saturation.

The campaign minimum scope includes dependency admission and projection. Dogfood proves a projection defect. Instead of repairing it, the campaign narrows scope to admission only and reclassifies the already-proved projection defect as unrelated follow-up work so it can claim saturation.

The campaign initially covers a serializer and its public API. During repair, evidence proves persisted round-trip behavior is directly affected by the same semantic change, but the campaign refuses to expand scope to persistence because it was not named at the start, then claims saturation.

Candidate A passes fresh dogfood. The branch is rebased onto a newer authoritative base that changes dependencies inside the campaign surface, but the campaign reuses A's scope assumptions, probe evidence, and qualification authority without re-establishing them, then claims completion.

The campaign initially establishes the repository's canonical verify-and-package workflow as final qualification. The candidate then edits that workflow to remove the package gate and validates itself against the weakened candidate workflow without independent admission against the previous authority, then ends SATURATED.

Dogfood reproduces an in-scope defect whose semantic owner is an upstream dependency. To keep the campaign on one branch, the downstream project adds a local workaround that masks the upstream defect and then claims saturation without repairing or qualifying the upstream owner.

The campaign freezes a minimum semantic scope and establishes final qualification authority. It proves several defects, repairs them, and later evidence shows one directly affected persistence interaction, so scope expands monotonically. A fresh-pass probe contract grows by one probe before completion; already-completed probes remain valid on the same unchanged candidate, the added probe completes, no qualifying defect remains, and final validation passes.

Dogfood notices a suspicious adjacent code path but cannot reproduce a violated behavior or prove a material consequence. codebase-finding-derivation records INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, so the lead is preserved for later investigation but is not treated as a qualifying defect and does not by itself block saturation.

Repairs remain uncommitted during the deep loop. Before validation and dogfood, the campaign computes a deterministic identity over every exercised tracked, staged, untracked generated, and projected byte and records it with the evidence, so no checkpoint commit is needed.

Dogfood proves an in-scope defect is owned by an upstream library. The downstream campaign remains blocked while the upstream owner is repaired and qualified, then re-establishes downstream candidate evidence against the fixed upstream identity instead of adding a masking workaround.

Before the campaign begins, repository-owned policy explicitly states that this class of prompt-only change has no additional final validation beyond the required focused structural checks. The campaign completes those checks, saturates its semantic surface, records the authoritative final-validation set as empty, and ends SATURATED.

A new repository-wide discovery skill requires a reachable production path before reporting a finding, but its OUTPUT says 'No issues found' whenever a bounded grep returns nothing. It records no inspected scope, truncation, unavailable paths, or incomplete state.

A qualification skill says a candidate may choose the required test slices and pass threshold at evaluation time. The same candidate may edit those settings, rerun only the newly required checks, and declare itself qualified.

A narrow retry-idempotency skill owns one duplicate-effect failure class, requires a reproduced replay path before FINDING, names safe repeatable behavior in DO NOT REPORT, and makes no repository-wide absence claim. It does not carry source digests or environment identity because the bounded review result is not reused across mutable candidates.

A sensitive-data transformation skill is longer than most review skills because it defines masking categories, deterministic placeholder behavior, a second verification pass, fail-closed MASKING_INCOMPLETE, and a bounded transformation boundary. Its extra sections each carry unique safety semantics rather than repeating generic methodology.

The governing qualification contract requires correctness, ambiguity and non-edit slices. After seeing that ambiguity cases fail, the candidate redefines its claimed qualification scope to correctness-only and reports PASS from that smaller evidence set.

A repository-wide architecture triage inspects one controller directory, cannot access workers or persistence, finds no hotspot in that directory, and reports that the repository has no architecture risks requiring specialist review.

The previous qualification contract requires correctness, ambiguity and non-edit slices. The candidate edits that governing contract to remove ambiguity after ambiguity cases fail, then uses the candidate contract to declare its remaining evidence ready and qualified without independent admission of the policy change.

A repository wraps native uv lock authoring in a helper that first runs uv lock, then independently parses dependency metadata, maintains its own retry/cache state, rewrites the lock on selected failures, and reports its synthetic convergence result as dependency truth. No repository-specific policy requires those duplicated resolution semantics.

A repository launches native kubectl through a thin execution boundary that only binds an already-selected kubeconfig and cwd, applies a timeout and process-tree cancellation, captures stdout/stderr/exit status with provenance, and projects PASS/FAIL/INCOMPLETE. It does not reconstruct rollout, health, retry, selection, or Kubernetes state semantics.

A local working-tree candidate repairs a reproduced retained-evidence validation defect and its focused regression passes. The focused check is green, but no post-repair mutation, composition, identity, completeness, or cross-surface attack has run against the repaired candidate. The next action is being chosen.

During an adversarial repair campaign over a release-candidate directory, the next reproduced defect is proven to belong to a separately versioned upstream repository. Repairing it locally would require a downstream workaround that duplicates upstream semantics. Determine whether to keep patching the current candidate.

A frozen paired benchmark has verified immutable receipts for every selected definition, but one assisted trial is INCOMPLETE because the native MCP workspace binding could not be verified. The operator treats structural receipt completeness as qualification, counts that row as a product failure, and publishes the comparison.

After an assisted condition fails its frozen oracle, the campaign edits the prompt and answer key in the same experiment version, reruns only that condition, and combines the new receipt with the original bare control to claim improvement.

A frozen paired campaign re-establishes current harness authority, preflights the exact selected definitions, runs with matching bare controls, retains verified non-conflicting PASS/FAIL receipts under stable runtime authority, reports unavailable metrics as unavailable, and hands a reproduced product defect to a separate repair campaign without changing the experiment.
